rules.objective: The first partnership to reach nine points wins. Points are scored from tricks (one point per trick in excess of six) and from honours (AKQJ of trumps: two points for three honours, four points for all four).
rules.gameplay: Four players in two partnerships (partners opposite). Twelve cards each, dealt four at a time. Top card of the four-card stock determines trump. Holder of the Ace of trump (or dealer if Ace is exposed) ruffs by taking the stock and discarding four cards. Player to dealer's left leads; all follow suit if possible, otherwise may play any card. Trick is won by the highest trump, or if no trump played, by the highest card of the led suit. Twelve tricks per deal. Honours may be declared to end the game (except on eight points): declare three or more in hand, or with two call Can-ye for partner's honours.
keyRules: 17th-century English Whist ancestor; related to Ruff and Trump.
Follow suit if possible; trick won by highest trump or highest card of led suit.
One point per trick over six; honours (AKQJ of trumps) score two for three, four for all four.
First partnership to nine points wins.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Trump beats any non-trump; when no trump played, highest card of led suit wins.

edgeCases.text: Holder of Ace of trump (or dealer if Ace is exposed) takes the four-card stock and discards any four cards before play.

Except on eight points, a player may declare three or more honours in hand to end the deal, or with two honours call Can-ye for partner to contribute; honours score two for three, four for all four (AKQJ of trumps).

customActions.description: Lead any card to start a trick. First lead each deal is by the player to dealer's left; thereafter the trick winner leads.
customActions.constraints: Legal only when it is the player's turn to lead (first to play in the trick).

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
